overall: Strong semantic extraction: no wrong memo precedence, enum casing, band value, question order, deadline, callback value or same-day boolean observed. One scope-broadening wording error and several unsupported-rule encodings remain. Raw diff count is not a semantic error count.
expected_spec_note: Expected fixtures deliberately use current guide fields only. Unsupported arithmetic/routing/priority rules are preserved in prose, not invented executable keys. Arbitrary situation ids, optional explicit defaults, and wording are interpreted semantically rather than treating all diffs as failures.

suggested_spec_guide_edits.new: When the brief is raw material, order policy versions and amendments by their stated effective chronology, then apply each amendment field by field. A partial rollback restores only the explicitly named fields; retain all unrevoked earlier changes, including added holidays. Record the final value and its source in coverage. Code lists identify meanings, but exact request enum values in the supplied API are authoritative for wire spelling and case; map display aliases by meaning, never copy invalid codes.

suggested_spec_guide_edits.old: 4. `get_account` returns 1 to 3 late products. The agent states every product, asks for payment today.
suggested_spec_guide_edits.new: 4. `get_account` returns 1 to 3 late products. The agent states every product and makes the initial payment ask required by the brief. Never assume the initial date is today; a same-day prohibition also applies to the initial ask and voluntary offers.

suggested_spec_guide_edits.old: - `ask_today`, `ask_today_all`: the first ask for one product / for several products.
suggested_spec_guide_edits.new: - `ask_today`, `ask_today_all`: despite these historical names, copy the brief's exact INITIAL payment question for one product / several products. If today is forbidden, these must ask for the allowed future date, not today. Preserve the initial-date rule separately in negotiation_rules and coverage; text alone cannot configure the policy engine's initial acceptance date.

suggested_spec_guide_edits.old: `floor_percent` (when the floor is a percentage of the past-due amount instead of a field), `floor_min` (a minimum floor amount, if any)
suggested_spec_guide_edits.new: `floor_percent` (percentage points, e.g. 22.5 for 22.5%, based on the mapped past-due amount), `floor_min` (a minimum floor amount, if any). Preserve any specified rounding mode, precision or cap verbatim in negotiation_rules and coverage; do not claim that floor_percent alone implements upward/downward rounding because the current runtime rounds to nearest penny

suggested_spec_guide_edits.old: - `situations`: things the customer may say during the negotiation. Map of id -> object:
suggested_spec_guide_edits.new: - `situations`: map each distinct brief-defined situation to its own id, trigger and action, including new queues (e.g. an existing debt-management plan must not be merged with requesting a new plan). Capture the exact stages and precedence specified by the brief. Current effect handling runs during negotiation only: preserve a requirement for opening/security handling in global_rules and coverage and identify that it requires compiler support; global prose does not make an unavailable transfer tool callable.

suggested_spec_guide_edits.old: - `outcomes`: map of the generic outcomes `promise`, `paid`, `transferred`, `no_promise`, `not_verified`, `not_reached` -> the exact `outcome` codes of `close_call`. Add `partial_promise` only if the brief closes differently when a promised amount is below the full past-due amount.
suggested_spec_guide_edits.new: - `outcomes`: map the generic outcomes promise, paid, transferred, no_promise, not_verified and not_reached to exact close_call enum codes. Add partial_promise only if specified. Separately preserve the brief's precedence for mixed product outcomes/reasons verbatim in negotiation_rules and coverage; mappings alone cannot express a priority table and must not be treated as implementing one.

suggested_spec_guide_edits.old: - `coverage`: list of strings "rule <number or short name> -> <spec field>" for EVERY rule in the brief. Rules that no field can hold go into the closest `*_rules` list, word for word.
suggested_spec_guide_edits.new: - `coverage`: list a mapping for EVERY brief rule, including every retained amendment, exact sentence, API field rename and cross-stage exception. Where no executable field can implement a rule, preserve it verbatim in the closest *_rules list and label its coverage entry "UNSUPPORTED by current compiler: <rule> -> <needed field>". Do not count prose preservation as executable coverage. Request-field role renames require explicit compiler bindings; never assume request roles can be inferred from account response mappings.

verification_limits: Ran exactly the requested local extract_check harness once per brief (two LLM calls per run), not twice. Both compile and policy self-test completed without reported problems.

Self-test uses a fixed 2026-10-14 clock and only refuse-all / late-date scenarios. It does not exercise partial rollback holiday dates, penny-rounding boundaries, mixed-reason ordering, callback endpoints, early DMP routing, or request schema conformance.
No Freya APIs, deploys, simulations, chat, or live tool calls were made. Synthetic API hosts end in .invalid.
No runtime probes beyond the requested harness were executed. Additional compiler behavior claims are source-established implications, not observed transcripts or ledger results.
Only lab/stress was written; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 prevented importing the harness from creating pycache outside scratch.
